newsitem.title: CANADA: T. Eaton Co says files for creditor protection.
newsitem.headline: T. Eaton Co says files for creditor protection.

text.p: One of Canada's oldest department store retailers T. Eaton Co Ltd said on Thursday it has filed for court protection from its creditors as it tries to restructure its retail operations.
Eaton's said in a statement that it is seeking an Ontario court order under the Companies' Creditors Arrangement Act. The court application is limited to the company's retail operations.
The privately-owned, Toronto-based company said it also has arranged C$555 million in new financing from a major financial institution.
Company president George Eaton said the court application will allow the company to continue its day-to-day operations while negotiating a restructuring plan with its stakeholders.
"We view this as a temporary measure that gives us time to turn our situation around and move forward. Our goal is to emerge with a strong and viable network stores," Eaton said.

He said suppliers will be paid in full for goods and services delivered during this period. "We will have to vacate a number of stores over time. But it is too early to predict the future of specific stores or any other measures that may be taken," Eaton said.

T. Eaton Co Ltd is the retailing arm of the Eaton Group of Companies, which has been selling some of its real estate in recent years. A year ago the company sold real estate worth about C$300 million.

Wood Gundy analyst David Brodie said it was hard to tell how Eaton's would restructure as the family-held institution had been reluctant to discuss its operations in the past. "We've never had any figures on these guys," he said.
